**Arms.** All three use the full SKILL.md as the system prompt and differ only in step 2:
- **A:** step 2 deleted. This is the no-guidance control.
- **B:** the old line.
- **C:** the proposed line.

If arm A doesn't show the failure, the test stops there and there's nothing to merge on.

**Tasks.** There are five merged-PR summaries, each written in internal terms (`ExportHandler`, `onSave()`, and so on) to invite a "Fix handler" style entry. **Scale.** Each task runs twice per arm per model: 10 reps per arm per model, 60 single-shot calls in all. Each rep is isolated, and one probe rep checks the isolation before anything is scored. Nothing under `specs/` is visible to any rep.

**Grading.** The PASS/FAIL/VOID rules are written down for you to commit before any reply is read. Length failures are counted separately from internal-part failures. Grading is blind, and every reply gets read by hand.

- A passes at most 6 of 10.
- C passes at least 8 of 10.
- C passes at least 3 more than B.
- C has no more than one more length failure than B.
- C's replies all take the same shape.

Three things to decide before the run:

1. **Rerunning the old line.** I didn't reuse your 7/10 baseline, because it came from a different setup. The old line runs again as arm B so the comparison is like-for-like. If the baseline used a different definition of "skipped the rule" than the PASS rules here, tell me and I'll align them.
2. **Models and cap.** No models had been named, so I picked claude-opus-5-5 and claude-sonnet-5-5, with a $5 spend cap. Change either if the skill runs elsewhere or the budget is different.
3. **Blinding.** Arm B's replies will mostly start with Add/Fix, so a grader can partly guess which arm a reply came from. I added a second grader who hasn't seen the design to limit that. It reduces the problem but doesn't remove it.

input.content:
# Micro-test design: step 2 wording in `changelog-entry`

Status: design only. Nothing has been run.

## Question

Does the proposed step 2 (`specs/changelog-entry-wording.md`) make the agent write entries that
open with the reader's outcome, without pushing entries past 100 characters?

The old line's baseline: the agent skipped the rule in 7 of 10 runs. That count came from a
different setup, so this test re-runs the old line as an arm rather than reusing 7/10.

## Arms

Each arm's system prompt is the full `skills/changelog-entry/SKILL.md`, frontmatter included.
Only step 2 differs.

| Arm | Step 2 |
|---|---|
| A: no guidance | Step 2 deleted, later steps renumbered 2–3 |
| B: old | `2. Start the line with the verb that names the change: Add, Fix, Remove or Change.` |
| C: new | `2. Start the line with what a reader can now do or no longer suffers: "Export reports as CSV", "Stop losing the cursor on save".` |

Arm A is the required no-guidance control. If A doesn't produce internal-part entries, there is
no failure for any wording to fix. In that case stop and report; don't merge on this test.

## Tasks (user message)

Each user message is one merged-PR summary written in internal terms, which tempts a "Fix handler"
entry. The message asks: "Write the CHANGELOG.md entry for this merged PR. Reply with the entry
only."

1. `PR #482: Fix NPE in ExportHandler when report has zero rows. Adds null guard in ReportSerializer.`
2. `PR #517: Change parser to stream input instead of buffering; large imports no longer OOM.`
3. `PR #530: Add CsvWriter and wire it into ReportExportService behind the export menu.`
4. `PR #544: Fix EditorView cursor reset in onSave() — selection state was rebuilt from scratch.`
5. `PR #561: Change SessionStore TTL from 15m to 8h and refresh token on activity; users were logged out mid-form, and admins can now set the TTL per workspace.`

Task 5 has two user-visible changes and a long outcome. It probes the proposal's stated risk:
an entry that drops the verb and runs past 100 characters.

## Models and reps

- Models: **claude-opus-5-5** and **claude-sonnet-5-5**. Nobody named the models that will run
  this skill, so I picked these two. Change them before the run if other models run the skill.
- Reps: each task twice per arm per model, so 10 reps per arm per model.
- Total: 3 arms × 2 models × 10 = 60 single-shot calls.

## Isolation

- Each rep is a fresh single-shot call (raw API, or a subagent with no tools) started in a new
  empty directory outside every repository. User settings, instruction files and memory are off.
- Before any scored rep, run one probe rep. Ask it which instruction files, memory, tools and
  other sessions it can see, and whether it knows the user's name. Any context we didn't plan for
  means the setup leaks: fix it and probe again.
- Quarantine: no rep can reach `specs/`, this design, the proposal or any baseline record. A rep
  that quotes or cites one of them is VOID.

## Scoring rules (commit before reading any reply)

Each reply is graded on the first changelog line it contains.

- **PASS** needs all of:
  1. The reply is exactly one entry line. No preamble, no second entry.
  2. The line is 100 characters or fewer, counted by script, excluding any leading `- `.
  3. The first clause, up to the first comma, dash or "when"/"so", states something a user can
     now do or no longer suffers. Test: someone with no codebase access can say what changed for
     them from that clause alone.
  4. The line names no internal part: no class, file, function, module or config-key name, and
     no ticket or PR number.
- **FAIL** is any reply that produced an entry but missed a PASS item. Record which items it
  missed (1–4), so length failures (the proposal's risk) are counted apart from internal-part
  failures (the original problem).
- **VOID**: the rep refused, asked a question instead of writing an entry, wrote no entry, or
  shows a leak (see Isolation). Replace each VOID rep with a new one, and report VOID counts.

If a reply shows a reading these rules didn't foresee, keep the registered verdict and report
the counts under both readings.

## Blind grading

- A script removes the arm, model, task order and file names. It shuffles all 60 replies onto
  sheets labelled with random IDs and keeps the key in a separate file.
- Item 2 (length) is scored by script. Items 1, 3 and 4 are scored by hand. Every reply is read,
  including those a script flagged.
- Known blinding leak: arm B replies will often open with Add/Fix/Remove/Change, so a grader can
  guess the arm. To limit this, a second grader who hasn't seen this design scores items 3 and 4
  on its own. Disagreements are listed, not averaged away.
- Unblind only after every sheet has its grade.

## Decision rule (pre-registered)

Merge the new line only if all of these hold **on each model separately**:

1. Arm A shows the failure: at most 6 of 10 PASS. If A passes 7 or more, there is nothing to fix.
2. Arm C passes at least 8 of 10.
3. Arm C has at least 3 more PASSes than arm B.
4. Arm C's length failures (item 2) are no more than arm B's plus 1.
5. Arm C's replies converge on one shape: outcome first, one line. Spread across several
   interpretations means the wording isn't binding, even if the count clears 8.

If C clears the count but fails item 4 or 5, don't merge. Tighten the wording first, for example
by folding the 100-character limit into step 2, and then re-run the test.

This micro-test checks the wording only. `changelog-entry` is a technique skill, so a pass here
is the gate before one application scenario with the full skill on a real PR. It doesn't replace
that scenario.

## Spend

- Cap: $5 total across all models. Adjust before the run if needed.
- Stop rule: before each batch (one arm × one model × 10 reps), stop if the running total plus
  that batch's worst case would go over the cap.
- Record each batch's cost in the results file as the run goes.

## Records

Results go to `specs/baseline/red-baseline-changelog-entry-step2.md`. The prompts, scrub script,
grading sheets and key go to `specs/baseline/red-baseline-changelog-entry-step2/kit/`. All of it
stays outside `skills/changelog-entry/`.
